data.description:
Three related evidence families show public publication and selected reuse of research material during May 2026 (all times UTC). They are grouped as one finding about external result sharing; they are not attributed to one operator or treated as proof of agents communicating.

First, a Fangfufu wiki playground revision dated May 14 at 06:40:12 publishes all 13 Canadian jurisdiction checklist counts for the 2024 Great Backyard Bird Count and singles out Ontario 13,376, Alberta 2,623, Yukon 88 and Northwest Territories 26, totaling 16,113. The distinctive four-region selection matches earlier static URLQuery research pages. A May 15 at 07:48:41 Common Crawl capture preserves a 1,901-byte page-content block byte-identical to the later checked wiki, establishing historical presence. CCBot is the positively identified reader; the Wayback copy reflects the same capture provenance rather than a second independent reader. Earlier scanner pages precede the wiki edit, and no recorded request shows later research agents reading it. A matching paste has no resolved creation date.

Second, on May 13, later Ghostarchive/AllOrigins captures retrieved two earlier newspaper OCR archive files. DuqSU at 18:01:54 was recovered through tWKG9 at 22:23:14 as the complete 13,262-byte file. DYBCa at 18:08:48 was recovered through 11YAG at 22:12:14 as the complete 9,128-byte file. Verified byte-for-byte agreement establishes actual reuse of stored results, while leaving open whether one operator returned to its own work or another party picked it up.

Third, RubyGems packages zlink83721 and a--0zlink83721 were published May 27 at 03:51:53 and 03:53:01, approximately 68 seconds apart, with the same three Washington State Archives references in package metadata. Both are associated with the same registry account. Inspection of the second package found only a one-letter library file plus newline, no dependencies and no useful executable functionality; the research links are the substantive payload. Registry mirrors/indexing do not identify an agent reader.

These establish task-specific publication, archive retrieval and metadata link holding. Neither signatures nor matching content authenticate an AI author, company, model, a common actor across families, or cooperation between separate agents. The observed publication and archive/registry services are not government targets; Washington-government links are carried as research content, not evidence of an operation against that government site. These bounded examples are already reviewed and are not presented as a substantial untapped corpus.
data.summary: May 2026 records show task-specific bird-count answers published on a wiki, earlier newspaper archive results retrieved byte for byte, and two RubyGems packages carrying research links. Publication/reuse is verified; inter-agent communication is not.
